description:
Programme or Project Overview

The Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in biophysics. The position addresses quantitative questions about the structure, dynamics and interactions of biological molecules, using methods that may include optical and single-molecule spectroscopy, computational modelling and advanced biochemical assays. Doctoral researchers in the department's biophysics groups work at the boundary of physics and biology, and the employment is a salaried four-year contract under the Swedish collective agreement.

The department offers a well-instrumented research environment with access to core facilities and the Stockholm life-science ecosystem, including Science for Life Laboratory. Doctoral students receive training in experimental and computational biophysics, participate in international collaborations and build a publication record that supports later research careers in academia or industry. The specific project direction is agreed with the supervisory group from the department's current biophysics portfolio.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in biophysics, physics, biochemistry or a related quantitative field, and bring strong analytical skills and an interest in molecular-level questions. Programming experience and familiarity with instrumentation are advantages. Applications are made through Stockholm University's Varbi portal with a CV, degree transcripts, contact details for references and a brief statement of research interests.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD employment in biophysics
  • Single-molecule and quantitative molecular methods
  • Physics-biology interface research environment
  • Access to SciLifeLab and departmental core facilities
  • International collaboration and conference support
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
